findings.title: Client removal no longer cleans up V2 permissions; V1+V2 combination throws on delete
Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is not found
findings.body:
`getResourceTypeResource` returns null in several cases, for example when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false because the realm has admin permissions disabled or the 'Clients' resource is missing. `root.realmResourceServer()` can still be non-null in that case.

The result is passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)` and then used as `resource.getScopes()`. Any client permission check for a client without its own resource then throws a NullPointerException instead of returning false.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns wrong names / misses per-client resources
findings.body:
Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(...)` without setting a type. Only the 'Clients' type resource has type `Clients`.

As a result, `findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` never finds individual client resources. It can only return the type resource itself, whose name is the literal string "Clients", not a client id.

Callers relying on `getClientsWithPermission` therefore get an empty set or a bogus id instead of the clients the admin is actually allowed to access.

findings.title: All-clients VIEW short-circuits per-client deny permissions
findings.body:
`canView(ClientModel)` returns true as soon as `canView()` is true. `canView()` checks the all-clients VIEW permission.

Because of this, a per-client permission that denies VIEW (NEGATIVE logic or a negative policy) on a specific client is never evaluated. The pattern of granting all and denying one, which is supported and tested for users (`testViewUserPermission`), does not work for clients and over-grants access.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for Clients resource type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` only maps USERS resources to readable names. For the newly added CLIENTS type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`.

Per-client resources are created with no display name and are named by the client internal UUID. The "Clients" all-resource is also not mapped to an "All clients" label.

Consumers such as the admin UI will show null or a UUID instead of the clientId.

findings.title: Javadoc for void require* methods says 'Returns true'
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireView()` (line 95) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100) says "Returns {@code true} if ...". Both methods are void and throw ForbiddenException on failure, as the other `require*` docs describe.

findings.title: Tests leave state behind (roles, client name, client scopes) without cleanup
findings.body:
These tests permanently mutate the shared managed realm and never register any cleanup:
- `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates the client roles 'myclient-role' and 'myclient-subRole' on myclient. The returned Responses are not closed or checked.
- `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames myclient/realmClient and moves default client scopes to optional.

Other tests, or reruns, may see altered state. For example, `getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` may refer to a different scope, and role creation would return 409.
